questions.subject: MODERN_PHYSICS
questions.learningObjective: Solve a quantitative quarks and fundamental particles problem by applying the governing physical principle.
questions.stem: An unstable resonance has a decay width of 1 MeV. Approximately what is its lifetime?

options.misconception: Assumes a linear rather than inverse-square or exponential relation

questions.explanation: The uncertainty relation links width and lifetime: tau is approximately hbar divided by the decay width Gamma. With Gamma = 1 MeV converted to joules, tau = hbar/Gamma = 6.58 × 10^-16 seconds. Doubling, halving, or adding a factor of ten each misapply the width-lifetime relation.
questions.hint: Use tau approximately equal to hbar divided by the energy width.
